title: Strategic Management
sources_used: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: BYJU’S was founded in 2011 and launched its learning application in 2015. Demand for online education increased sharply during the COVID-19 pandemic, and the company expanded into more than 21 countries while acquiring several education businesses. Its valuation rose from approximately $5 billion before the pandemic to $22 billion in 2022. Difficulties later emerged when the company delayed filing its financial statements for the year ended ; Deloitte resigned as auditor after stating that it had not received the required documents, and three investor representatives left the board. The Board of Control for Cricket in India initiated insolvency proceedings over unpaid sponsorship dues of approximately $19 million, while US lenders claimed that they were owed about $1 billion. In August 2024, India’s Supreme Court revived insolvency proceedings, and Reuters subsequently reported claims exceeding $1.5 billion from 1,887 creditors. Founder Byju Raveendran later acknowledged that the company had entered too many markets too quickly and stated that its value had fallen to zero. . Define strategy implementation and list four factors that influence its effectiveness. (b). Explain how the events presented in the BYJU’S case are connected with the implementation of strategy. (c). Assume that you were appointed to lead BYJU’S in 2022 before the crisis became severe. Present the three actions you would have taken first and justify them using information from the case. Long Essay A choice between two options for each question, answer two short essay questions, one from each pair
questions.solution_html:
• Provides long-term direction and defines goals for the organisation.
  • It is an agreement between two or more firms to cooperate for mutual benefit.
  • It involves huge data collection and can cause information overload and analysis paralysis.
  • Corporate-Level Strategy
  • Formulated by top management Board. It decides the overall scope and direction.
  • Decides which businesses to enter, retain or exit.
  • Corporate-Level Strategy
  • Formulated by Top Management - Mukesh Ambani and Board.
  • Decides overall scope, which industries to enter or exit.
  • Reliance Example
  • Reliance started as textile, then corporate strategy decided to diversify into
  • Petrochemicals & Refining (Jamnagar Refinery)
  • Jio Telecom (2016)
  • Reliance Retail
  • Green Energy (2021)
  • Environmental Scanner: Manager monitors internal and external environment using PESTLE and
  • SWOT to identify opportunities and threats.
  • Industry Attractiveness (Y-Axis): How attractive is the industry to invest? It is measured by
  • Market factors: Size, growth rate, seasonality.
  • Competition: Number of rivals, entry barriers.
  • Financial: Profitability, ROI.
  • PESTLE factors: Government regulations, technology.
  • No major change: Continues with same products and customers.
  • When environment is stable: No major opportunity or threat.
  • Organizational Structure: The structure must match strategy. If company expands to 21
  • countries and many businesses, it needs divisional, matrix or SBU structure with proper control.
  • BYJU'S structure became too complex and unmanageable.
  • Failure of Structural Implementation - Over-expansion
  • Valuation rose from $5B to $22B. But implementation requires integrating these acquisitions.
  • BYJU'S failed to integrate, structure became too wide. Founder himself said "entered too many
  • markets too quickly" - shows poor implementation of corporate-level growth strategy.
